title: Verified knapsack rounding guarantees for nested-logit assortments
contribution_type: complete formalization of two established approximation inequalities
claim: Every optimal continuous knapsack solution with at most one fractional item gives the exact factor-two utility bound using its rounded set and optional fractional singleton. If each item occupies at most epsilon of capacity, the rounded set gives the exact1/(1-epsilon) utility bound under the one-fractional-item condition.
assumptions: Finite product set and nested-logit utility v_ij(r_ij-u), with u>=0, zero within-nest no-purchase weight, positive preference and space weights, and each item individually fitting the capacity.
The supplied continuous LP point is optimal with coordinates in[0,1] and total space at most capacity. Equation11 records its zero-or-one fractional coordinate by an Option index.
The refined guarantee assumes one fractional coordinate,0<=epsilon<1, and every item space<=epsilon*capacity. Complete target statements are linked and retained without weakened binders.
supporting_scope: Selected coordinates have nonnegative utility, derived by a feasible improving-deletion argument.
Exact objective splitting treats the integral and fractional cases separately.
A feasible perturbation gives c*a_j<=w_j*OPT; this handles zero-utility fractional coordinates without assuming capacity exhaustion or dividing by the rounded objective.

formal_targets.contribution_scope: Complete two-approximation inequality for every optimal LP point with optional fractional coordinate, including integral and nonpositive-utility cases; no candidate-family cardinality claim.
Complete small-item 1/(1-epsilon) rounding guarantee for any optimal LP point with one fractional coordinate, including zero utility; candidate-family construction remains separate.
